run.question:
Our US prod cluster is having a checkout incident — investigate using
app-262-prod-logs.

report.summary: Only one data source this run holds evidence about the US production cluster: the Elasticsearch index app-262-prod-logs (its documents carry a `cluster` field). Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) on every attempt, so no error rates, latency readings, spans or alert state could be checked. In that index the whole authorized window contains exactly 5 documents: three ERROR lines from cluster production-us-east-1 (checkout-service twice, payment-service once) forming a chain — checkout POST /api/checkout failing on a 30s payment-provider timeout named Stripe-US at 2026-11-22T07:47:00Z, payment-service reporting `Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms` at 08:47:00Z, and checkout-service reporting `Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 44%)` at 09:17:00Z — plus two INFO healthy lines from a different cluster, production-eu-west-1. The deepest dependency the evidence names is the external payment provider `stripe-us` (/v1/charges), reached through payment-service; the 44% failure rate and the circuit-breaker state are quoted from a log message, not measured, and whether the 30s timeout sits in the provider or in payment-service's egress path is not distinguishable from these lines. The Kubernetes cluster I can read is not identified as production-us-east-1: the only cluster identity its own telemetry carries is the alert-rule label `cluster: opspilot-m1`, its services are named checkout/payment (the US logs say checkout-service/payment-service), it has no stripe service/endpoint and the payment deployment has no external provider address. In that cluster all otel-demo payment/checkout pods are Running and ready, endpoints exist, and the pods' own logs show completed charges and completed orders at 08:48:40, 09:17:47 and 09:18:39 UTC — i.e. at the minutes the US log lines report failures — so that readable cluster is treated as a different, checked-and-healthy environment, not as impact of this incident and not as disproof of it. No Kubernetes object is seen applying a payment fault: the flagd flags paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable are ENABLED with defaultVariant `off`, and no otel-demo workload restarted during the window.

claims.text: The Elasticsearch source holds exactly one index, app-262-prod-logs (5 documents, 7.1kb), and its mapping is cluster, level, message, service, timestamp (all keyword except message text and timestamp date).

Searched over the whole authorized window (2026-11-21T09:47:08Z to 2026-11-22T09:47:08Z on field `timestamp`, sorted ascending), app-262-prod-logs matched exactly 5 documents with writer timestamps 2026-11-22T07:47:00Z to 09:17:00Z: three level=ERROR documents from cluster production-us-east-1 (service checkout-service twice, service payment-service once) and two level=INFO documents from cluster production-eu-west-1 (service checkout-service).

First US-cluster error (timestamp 2026-11-22T07:47:00Z, cluster production-us-east-1, service checkout-service, level ERROR): "POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (Stripe-US)".

Second US-cluster error (timestamp 2026-11-22T08:47:00Z, cluster production-us-east-1, service payment-service, level ERROR): "Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms" — the exact diagnostic text naming the timed-out upstream call to stripe-us /v1/charges at 30s.

Third US-cluster error (timestamp 2026-11-22T09:17:00Z, cluster production-us-east-1, service checkout-service, level ERROR): "Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 44%)" — the 44% figure is the text of this log message only.

The only healthy entries in the index come from a different cluster: cluster production-eu-west-1, service checkout-service, level INFO — "Healthy: p95 latency 230ms" at 2026-11-22T08:47:00Z and "Healthy: success rate 99.7%" at 09:17:00Z.

In the Kubernetes cluster I can read, the otel-demo workloads are all fully available: deployments checkout and payment each report readyReplicas=1 of replicas=1 (as do all 21 otel-demo deployments), pods checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n and payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d are phase Running with ready=true, started 2026-11-20T16:32:07Z (before the incident window) with container restartCount=2, and the payment and checkout Services have populated Endpoints (payment 10.244.0.5:8080, checkout 10.244.0.7:8080).

The only cluster identity carried by that cluster's own telemetry is the alert-rule label set on alert CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh in rule group opspilot-lab: labels cluster: opspilot-m1 and opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909, with expression (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name)(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m]))) / (same without status filter) > 0.5 for 2m.

In the readable cluster the checkout pod logged successful orders throughout the period around the asserted US failures: "[PlaceOrder]" followed by "payment went through (transaction_id: ...)" and "order confirmation email sent" at 09:10:54.18Z, 09:11:01.12Z, 09:11:46.59Z, 09:12:20.83Z, 09:14:19.16Z, 09:16:11.61Z, 09:17:47.24Z, 09:18:39.19Z, 09:19:23.78Z, 09:20:24.87Z, 09:21:46.04Z, 09:22:02.81Z, 09:23:32.57Z and 09:24:13.01Z.

In the readable cluster the payment pod logged "Charge request received." followed by "Transaction complete." for charged transactions between 2026-11-22T08:41:37Z and 08:54:37Z, including 08:45:29Z, 08:46:15Z, 08:46:32Z, 08:46:49Z, 08:48:40Z, 08:49:53Z, 08:50:28Z, 08:51:17Z and 08:53:21Z.

Filtering the payment pod's logs for err|error|fail|timeout|stripe|circuit|panic|exception over the authorized window (325 lines of the current container read) returned a single line: "(node:24) MetadataLookupWarning: received unexpected error = Invalid response from metadata service: incorrect Metadata-Flavor header. code = UNKNOWN" at 2026-11-22T08:04:24.937Z; no stripe/charge-timeout line was returned from that pod.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config holds demo.flagd.json in which the payment-related fault flags are paymentFailure (description "Fail payment service charge requests n%", state ENABLED, variants 100%:1, 90%:0.95, 75%:0.75, 50%:0.5, 25%:0.25, 10%:0.1, off:0, defaultVariant "off") and paymentUnreachable (description "Payment service is unavailable", state ENABLED, variants on:true/off:false, defaultVariant "off"); productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad are also defaultVariant "off".

The readable cluster's payment deployment (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment) has env PAYMENT_PORT=8080, FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013 and no external payment-provider address, while checkout (demo:2.0.2-checkout) has PAYMENT_ADDR=payment:8080; the otel-demo Services list contains no stripe service and the Endpoints list contains only payment/checkout/flagd among those checked.

The 19 events inside the window contain no eviction, OOMKill or crash-loop evidence: they are Normal Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started/Killing/SuccessfulCreate/ScalingReplicaSet activity for app-101 pods loki-66445c6d6f-cz9mq (Started 09:46:28Z) and payment-api-101-8486559b69-kkjmj (Started 09:46:49Z, containers stopped 09:47:02Z), plus two Warning FailedToCreateEndpoint events for other namespaces: service orca in app-95 ("endpoints \"orca\" already exists", 09:21:00Z) and service signup-service in app-162 (same message, 09:32:52Z).

At query time app-101 contains only pod loki-66445c6d6f-cz9mq (Running, started 2026-11-22T09:46:25Z, owner ReplicaSet loki-66445c6d6f) and the only app-101 deployment is loki (grafana/loki:2.9.0, 1/1); no payment-api-101 deployment or pod remains.

At the same minutes that the index records production-us-east-1 failures, the readable Kubernetes cluster's own pods succeeded: checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n logged "payment went through" at 09:17:47.24Z (just after the 09:17:00Z circuit-breaker line) and 09:18:39.19Z, and payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d logged "Transaction complete." at 08:48:40.85Z (just after the 08:47:00Z stripe-us timeout line). This cluster's checkout/payment therefore did not show the incident, which is why its healthy state is not used as evidence about production-us-east-1.

The index mixes two clusters: the two healthy checkout-service INFO lines are labelled cluster production-eu-west-1, while the three ERROR lines are labelled production-us-east-1, so the healthy readings describe a different cluster and are not evidence that the US cluster's checkout was healthy.

Rejected for the environment I could inspect: that the payment failure was caused by the flagd payment fault injections. Both paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable are state ENABLED but carry defaultVariant "off" (no targeting overrides in demo.flagd.json), and no otel-demo pod restarted during the window (checkout and payment pods started 2026-11-20T16:32:07Z, before the window), so no workload restart with an unchanged pod template coincided with this incident there.

Rejected as the explanation inside the readable cluster: pod-level failure of checkout or payment (crash, OOMKill, eviction, BackOff, failed health probe). Both pods are Running with ready=true and stable restart counts, all otel-demo deployments report 1/1 replicas ready, and the payment and checkout Service Endpoints are populated with those pods.

Probable chain in cluster production-us-east-1, supported only by application log text: payment-service's call to the external provider stripe-us (/v1/charges) exceeded 30s, checkout-service's own call then failed on the payment provider timeout (07:47:00Z), payment-service recorded the upstream timeout (08:47:00Z), and checkout's circuit breaker opened against payment-service at a reported 44% failure rate (09:17:00Z). The deepest named dependency is stripe-us, not a Kubernetes object.

Unresolved alternative for the same US-cluster timeouts: the 30s failure could sit in payment-service's egress path (DNS resolution, connection setup, network path or a proxy between the cluster and stripe-us) rather than in the provider itself. The log line states only that the call to stripe-us /v1/charges timed out; no client-span, DNS or network evidence was obtainable this run to separate these.

Working hypothesis on environment identity: the Kubernetes cluster I can read is not production-us-east-1 but the lab cluster its own telemetry labels cluster=opspilot-m1 — services are named checkout/payment rather than the index's checkout-service/payment-service, there is no stripe service/endpoint, and the payment deployment has no external provider address. Its healthy readings therefore neither confirm nor refute US-cluster impact, and no pod-level evidence for production-us-east-1 was available.

Obtain payment-service client spans (or a 30s-timeout histogram) for the stripe-us /v1/charges call and span status for checkout CheckoutService/PlaceOrder to establish onset, duration and the true failure ratio, and check Stripe-US provider status/latency for 2026-11-22 07:00-09:30Z; also collect us-east-1 egress/DNS data before deciding between a provider-side outage and a network-path cause.

Restore Prometheus and Jaeger access so CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh (the opspilot-lab rule computed from traces_span_metrics_calls_total status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR" for service_name="checkout", span_name CheckoutService/PlaceOrder) and the checkout circuit-breaker state can be evaluated, and extend the log index beyond 5 documents so onset/recovery and blast radius in production-us-east-1 can be measured rather than inferred from single lines.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable throughout the run: get_metric_names, get_all_labels, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_prometheus_target and list_prometheus_rules each returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error rate, latency, rpc_grpc_status, traces_span_metrics status_code or alert firing/pending state was checked; whether CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh was firing is unknown.

Jaeger was unavailable throughout the run: traces_list_services and traces_search both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no checkout/payment span graph, span error status, parent-child call edge to a stripe upstream, or latency baseline exists in this Run.

The index app-262-prod-logs contains only 5 documents and identifies work only through the `cluster` keyword (production-us-east-1, production-eu-west-1); it carries no pod, host, region code, environment or trace identifiers, so the incident's onset, recovery, request counts and blast radius in production-us-east-1 are unknown, and per-pod health for that cluster could not be checked.

No Kubernetes object or telemetry attribute ties the readable Kubernetes cluster to production-us-east-1; the only cluster identity observed is the alert-rule label cluster=opspilot-m1 (node opspilot-m1-control-plane). Whether that cluster is one of the two clusters in the index is unresolved, and its pods' short log retention (payment ~08:41Z onward, checkout ~09:10Z onward within the read) means the 07:47Z period could not be inspected there.

Whether the production-us-east-1 circuit breaker is still open, and when paymentFailure/paymentUnreachable or any other fault setting was last changed for the US cluster, is unknown: the flagd-config read reflects the readable cluster only, and the change_history integration is not integrated in this Run.
Kubernetes queries for networkpolicies and resourcequotas returned no_data (0 objects processed), so exhaustion or policy blocking in the readable cluster is unchecked, not observed-absent.

Only application log lines evidence the cause; no metric, trace or change record corroborates the stripe-us timeout, and the 44% failure rate is a figure inside a checkout log message rather than a measured value.
next_steps: Pull payment-service client-side metrics/spans for the stripe-us /v1/charges call in production-us-east-1 for 2026-11-22T07:30-09:30Z to separate provider latency from cluster egress/DNS problems.
Check the external Stripe-US provider's status and latency for the same window and whether a provider-side incident or credential/endpoint change was announced.
Evaluate CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh and the checkout-to-payment circuit-breaker state once Prometheus and Jaeger are reachable, and confirm when the breaker closed.
Review change records for production-us-east-1 payment configuration and any flagd targeting overrides for the US cluster, since the fault-setting values for that cluster could not be read.

content.alerting:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
